title: Azure, AWS or GCP OIDC is configured but the API-proxy adapter does not bind it to its upstream
symptoms: Provider requests fail with 404 "OpenAI proxy not configured" (or the equivalent not-configured response) although AWF_AUTH_TYPE=github-oidc and AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=azure, aws or gcp are set
The api-proxy logs a cloud_oidc_not_bound event (info) or a cloud_oidc_target_refused event (warn) when the adapter is created
conditions: AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER is azure, aws or gcp (native openai and anthropic workload identity are not affected)

The adapter's upstream is its default, or is a first-party host (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, *.githubcopilot.com, copilot-api.*.ghe.com), or its origin differs from COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL or from the other explicitly configured *_API_TARGET origins
This is a configuration-shape problem, not a token-exchange or Actions permission failure; do not change id-token permissions or rotate credentials for it
rootCause: The sidecar attaches cloud-issued OIDC credentials only to an adapter whose upstream is the explicitly configured cloud target, so a cloud token is never sent to a first-party provider host. resolveCloudOidcProviders() skips initialization when the adapter does not opt in (allowCloudOidc), when the target is a refused first-party host, or when the target origin does not match the selected origin (COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL first, otherwise all explicit *_API_TARGET values must share one origin). GCP is the exception: with no explicit target it remains available to the default Gemini and Vertex endpoints.

probe.expect: Run while the containers are kept (--keep-containers). A match names the adapter and target host and confirms the binding rule, not an authentication failure. Do not print request headers, docker inspect output or the container environment.

action: Set the upstream for the adapter that should use the cloud credential (for example COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL for Azure BYOK, or OPENAI_API_TARGET / ANTHROPIC_API_TARGET / the Gemini or Vertex target) to the same cloud origin, and do not point cloud OIDC at a first-party provider host. Native OpenAI and Anthropic workload identity use AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=openai or anthropic instead. Never work around this by exposing the Actions OIDC variables or exchanged credentials to the agent. A shipped release containing this behavior is not verified here.

references.title: api-proxy: bind cloud OIDC credentials to the configured upstream
